fixes.explanation: That's the crew. The LORD says, "Take some of the elders of the people and leaders of the priests…" (Jeremiah 19:1). Elders and priestly leaders are the ones named to go along. Jeremiah gets a jar and some company for the road trip.

The king isn't named on this guest list, friend. The LORD tells Jeremiah, "Take some of the elders of the people and leaders of the priests…" (Jeremiah 19:1). Elders and priestly leaders are the ones the text names. The kings of Judah are the ones Jeremiah is told to address (Jeremiah 19:3).

Moab isn't who this message is addressed to. The LORD says, "Hear the word of the LORD, O kings of Judah and residents of Jerusalem." (Jeremiah 19:3). That line names the kings of Judah and the residents of Jerusalem. Moab doesn't show up in it, friend.

Egypt isn't the one being addressed here. The LORD tells Jeremiah to proclaim, "Hear the word of the LORD, O kings of Judah and residents of Jerusalem." (Jeremiah 19:3). The message names the kings of Judah and the residents of Jerusalem. Egypt isn't in that line.

Right, it's false. The LORD says they burned incense to other gods "…that neither they nor their fathers nor the kings of Judah have ever known." (Jeremiah 19:4). So their fathers and the kings did not know these gods. Those are the gods the incense went to.

That's what the LORD says. "All who pass by will be appalled and will scoff at all her wounds." (Jeremiah 19:8). The people passing by react with shock and scoffing. I think this part stings, because the city ends up an object of scorn.

Binding up wounds isn't in this picture. The LORD says, "All who pass by will be appalled and will scoff at all her wounds." (Jeremiah 19:8). So the people walking by will be appalled and will scoff. Helping isn't what the verse describes.

That's it. The LORD says the houses were those "…on whose rooftops they burned incense to all the host of heaven and poured out drink offerings to other gods." (Jeremiah 19:13). So the rooftops held both the incense and the drink offerings. Both were offered to gods other than the LORD.

The text doesn't mention praying toward the house of the LORD. It says the rooftops were where "…they burned incense to all the host of heaven and poured out drink offerings to other gods." (Jeremiah 19:13). So the incense and drink offerings named there were for the host of heaven and other gods.

The Benjamin Gate isn't named in this passage. The text says Jeremiah "…stood in the courtyard of the house of the LORD and proclaimed to all the people…" (Jeremiah 19:14). So the place named is the LORD's house, with all the people there to hear.

True. Jeremiah proclaims what the LORD of Hosts says: "…I am about to bring on this city and on all the villages around it every disaster I have pronounced against them…" (Jeremiah 19:15). So it isn't only Jerusalem, because the villages around it are named too. The announcement names the city and its villages together.

It's true, friend. Jeremiah proclaims what the LORD of Hosts says: "…I am about to bring on this city and on all the villages around it every disaster I have pronounced against them…" (Jeremiah 19:15). The villages around Jerusalem are named right alongside the city. This part of the message reaches the whole area.
